definition_zh: 欢迎；迎接；受欢迎的；可随意使用的
definition_en: to greet someone in a friendly way, and to be gladly received or freely allowed
core_image: 院门被推开，主人快步迎出来，伸手接过客人的行李
scene: 第一次到同学家，他母亲在门口等着，接过包，说路上辛苦了，快进来。His mother met me at the door, took my bag and welcomed me inside.
sceneCN: 这里 welcome 是「欢迎」（第 1 个义项：友善地迎接某人）；句意为他母亲在门口接了我，接过包把我迎进屋。推门而出、伸手接手提行李的主人就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 受欢迎的；可随意使用的

collocations.zh: 欢迎来到我们这座城市

senses.title: To greet someone gladly
senses.definition: to meet a person in a friendly way and show that one is glad they came
senses.definitionCN: 友善地迎接某人，并表现出对他们的到来感到高兴
senses.example: They welcomed the guests at the gate with tea.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在门口用茶迎接客人。
senses.why: This is the core sense: the friendly meeting at arrival.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义：到访时友善的迎接。

senses.title: To be glad to accept
senses.definition: to receive an idea, a change or a gift with pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 愉快地接受某个想法、变化或礼物
senses.example: We welcome any suggestions for the new plan.
senses.exampleCN: 我们乐于接受对新计划的任何建议。
senses.why: A change can be greeted as a guest is, so the verb spreads to things.
senses.whyCN: 变化也能像客人一样被迎进来，于是动词扩展到事物。

senses.title: Received with pleasure
senses.definition: of news or events, gladly received
senses.definitionCN: 指消息或事件令人高兴
senses.example: The rain was welcome after a month of heat.
senses.exampleCN: 热了一个月之后，这场雨很受欢迎。
senses.why: The adjective describes what people would be glad to greet.
senses.whyCN: 形容词描述人们乐于迎接的东西。

senses.title: Freely permitted to use
senses.titleCN: 可随意使用的；受欢迎的（人）
senses.definition: of a person, allowed to do or take something without asking
senses.definitionCN: 指人无需请示即可使用或取用
senses.example: You are welcome to stay for dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 欢迎你留下吃晚饭。
senses.why: To be welcome somewhere is to be free of the usual barrier.
senses.whyCN: 在某处受欢迎，就是不受通常的界限阻挡。

senses.title: A greeting of arrival
senses.definition: the act of greeting, usually warm, in the noun form
senses.definitionCN: 名词形式，带来暖意的迎接行为
senses.example: They gave us a warm welcome at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在车站给了我们热烈的欢迎。
senses.why: The friendly meeting at the gate turned into a noun, so it became a thing one gives.
senses.whyCN: 门口那场友善的相见转为名词，于是成了一份可以送出的东西。

senses.title: A polite reply
senses.definition: a fixed reply to thanks, meaning there is no need to thank
senses.definitionCN: 对道谢的固定回答，意为不必谢
senses.example: “Thank you.” “You’re welcome.”
senses.exampleCN: “谢谢。”“不用谢。”
senses.why: The reply says the favour was freely given, so no debt remains.
senses.whyCN: 这句答语表示这份好意是白送的，因此不欠什么。

intro.en: Welcome is Old English wilcuma, a compound of will and come, meaning a guest whose coming is wished for.
intro.cn: welcome 是古英语 wilcuma，由 will 与 come 复合而成，意为「来得合人心愿的客人」。

items.en: Wilcuma named a desired guest, someone whose arrival pleased the host.
items.cn: wilcuma 指备受期盼的客人，其到来使主人高兴。

items.en: The first element is will, the wish, and the second is come, so the word literally means wished-coming.
items.cn: 第一部分是 will（意愿），第二部分是 come，字面即「如人所愿的到来」。

items.en: The noun was reshaped under the influence of French bienvenu and gave a verb welcome.
items.cn: 名词受法语 bienvenu 影响而变形，并衍生出动词 welcome。

items.en: The adjective sense of freely allowed appeared, as in you are welcome to try.
items.cn: 形容词「可随意」的义项出现，如 you are welcome to try。

items.en: You are welcome as a reply to thanks is recorded from the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 「不用谢」这一答语自十九世纪有记录。

note.en: The first group shares the welcome shape, the second gives the words used at a greeting.
note.cn: 第一组与 welcome 形近同族，第二组是迎接时的近义词。

entries.definition: Friendly to guests, or the act of greeting.
Not wanted or gladly received.
One who greets others.
The Old English ancestor, a wished-for guest.
entries.definitionCN: 古英语本源：受期盼的客人

entries.definition: To say hello to someone in a friendly way.
To meet and admit a guest, often formally.
Friendly care shown to guests.
To take what is offered.

normalIntro.en: Say the word slowly: will plus come, a coming that someone wishes for.
normalIntro.cn: 慢慢念这个词：will 加 come，一次有人盼望的到来。

normal.en: Welcome is verb, adjective and noun all at once.
normal.cn: welcome 可作动词、形容词和名词。

normal.en: You are welcome is the fixed reply to thanks.
normal.cn: You are welcome 是对道谢的固定回答。

normal.en: A warm welcome is the noun after an adjective.
normal.cn: a warm welcome 是形容词加名词。

normal.en: Unwelcome news is news nobody wanted.
normal.cn: unwelcome news 是没人想要的消息。

normal.en: Make someone welcome means put them at ease.
normal.cn: make someone welcome 是让某人自在。

abstract.en: Picture a gate swung open from inside.
abstract.cn: 想门从里面被推开。

abstract.en: Feel a bag lifted out of your hand.
abstract.cn: 感受手里的包被接走。

abstract.en: Hear the door close warmly behind you.
abstract.cn: 听门在身后温和地关上。

examples.en: They welcomed us with tea and fruit.
examples.cn: 他们用茶和水果欢迎我们。

examples.en: Your comments are welcome at any time.
examples.cn: 随时欢迎您提出意见。

examples.en: “Thanks for the lift.” “You’re welcome.”
examples.cn: “谢谢你载我一程。”“不客气。”

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维尔康」——维尔康先生每到门口就说：来得好，欢迎进屋。

root: 古英语 wilcuma（will 意愿 + cuma 来者，即受期盼的客人）→ 中古英语受法语 bienvenu 影响成 welcome。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as a wished-for arrival, becomes the act of greeting, then any glad acceptance and even the answer to thanks.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从「如人所愿的到来」出发，成为迎接的行为，再扩展到任何乐意的接受，乃至道谢的答语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a host taking a guest’s bag at the gate.
core.cn: 核心意象：主人在门口接过客人的包。

branches.en: The greeting branch: guests met at the gate and a warm welcome.
branches.cn: 迎接分支：门口迎客与热烈欢迎。

branches.en: The acceptance branch: suggestions and rain both welcome.
branches.cn: 接受分支：建议与雨都受欢迎。

branches.en: The permission branch: you are welcome to stay.
branches.cn: 许可分支：欢迎你留下。

branches.en: The reply branch: you’re welcome.
branches.cn: 答语分支：不用谢。

branches.en: The host and the permission branch: one opens a door, the other a choice.
branches.cn: 主人分支与许可分支：一个开门，一个放行。

intro.en: Welcome is a very old compound that can now be a verb, an adjective or a noun.
intro.cn: welcome 是很古老的复合词，如今可作动词、形容词或名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin used gratus and acceptare for being welcome, and the table gives those cousins.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 gratus 与 acceptare 表示受欢迎与被接受，拉丁表给出这些亲族词。

definition_zh: 井；水井；油井；（用作感叹或停顿）嗯、那么；很好地
definition_en: a deep hole dug or drilled into the ground to reach water, oil or gas, and also the old adverb of good, kept in idioms
core_image: 村口一块圆石井栏，辘轳上垂下一只木桶，井口冒着凉气
scene: 天刚亮，妇人摇着辘轳把木桶从井里提上来，水面上还浮着一层白雾。Every morning she draws a bucket of water from the old well behind the house.
sceneCN: 这里 well 是「水井」（第 1 个义项：为取水而向地下挖的深洞）；句意为她每天早上都从屋后那口老井里打上一桶水。石井栏、辘轳、冒凉气的井口就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: A hole dug for water
senses.definition: a deep hole in the ground, usually lined with stone or brick, from which water is drawn
senses.definitionCN: 在地上挖出的深洞，常用石块或砖砌壁，供人从中取水
senses.example: Every morning she draws a bucket of water from the old well behind the house.
senses.exampleCN: 她每天早上都从屋后那口老井里打一桶水。
senses.why: The oldest meaning of the word is simply this hole; in Old English wiell also covered a spring that bubbles up by itself.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的意思就是这个洞；古英语里的 wiell 同时也指自动涌出的泉水。

senses.title: A hole drilled for oil or gas
senses.definition: a deep bore made by machine in order to take oil, gas or water from far below the surface
senses.definitionCN: 用机械向地层深处钻出的孔道，用以获取石油、天然气或地下水
senses.example: The company shut down three wells when the price of oil fell.
senses.exampleCN: 油价下跌时，这家公司关掉了三口油井。
senses.why: Industry kept the shape of the old water hole and put it over any vertical shaft that taps a fluid underground.
senses.whyCN: 工业沿用了古老水井的形象，把任何伸向地下流体的竖直钻孔都叫作井。

senses.title: A source that keeps giving
senses.definition: in figurative use, a place or thing from which something seems to flow endlessly
senses.definitionCN: 比喻用法，指某种东西仿佛源源不断流出的来源
senses.example: Her letters are a well of stories about the old town.
senses.exampleCN: 她的来信是老城故事的源泉。
senses.why: A well never empties when you keep drawing from it, so the word became a picture of inexhaustible supply.
senses.whyCN: 只要不断打水，井也不会干，于是这个词成了取之不尽的供应之图像。

senses.title: In a good way
senses.definition: the adverb form of good, describing an action done in a skilful or pleasing manner
senses.definitionCN: good 的副词形式，说明某动作做得有技巧、令人满意
senses.example: She sings well for someone who has never had a lesson.
senses.exampleCN: 对一个从没上过课的人来说，她唱得很好了。
senses.why: This is a different word in origin, the adverb of good, which simply fell into the same spelling.
senses.whyCN: 这层意思来源不同，本是 good 的副词，只是拼写恰好合到了一起。

senses.title: In good health
senses.definition: used after a verb such as be or feel to say that someone is not ill
senses.definitionCN: 用在 be、feel 之后，表示某人身体没有病
senses.example: He was not well last week, so he stayed at home.
senses.exampleCN: 他上星期身体不舒服，所以待在家里。
senses.why: Health was once described as a state of being in good order, and the adverb simply filled that slot.
senses.whyCN: 健康过去被说成处于良好的状态，而这个副词正好占住了那个位置。

senses.title: A pause word at the start
senses.definition: spoken at the beginning of a remark to gain time or to soften what follows
senses.definitionCN: 说话开头使用，用来争取时间或让后面的话显得缓和
senses.example: Well, I am not sure that is the best plan.
senses.exampleCN: 嗯，我不确定那是不是最好的方案。
senses.why: The same short syllable is a place-holder, much like the opening of a conversation that needs a moment before it starts.
senses.whyCN: 同一个短音节被当作占位的声音，就像一句需要停顿片刻才开口的话的开头。

intro.en: Well as a water hole goes back to Old English wiell, a spring or a bubbling up, and it has been spelled well since the Middle English period.
intro.cn: 表示水井的 well 可追溯到古英语 wiell（泉、涌出），自中古英语时期起拼作 well。

items.en: Wiell meant a spring that came up out of the ground, and the word was used for any source of water.
items.cn: wiell 指从地下涌出的泉水，这个词也用来指任何水源。

items.en: A second word, wel, was the adverb meaning in a good way, and it stood beside the noun without any link.
items.cn: 另一个词 wel 是表示「良好地」的副词，它与名词并列存在，彼此并无联系。

items.en: In Middle English the two forms came to the same spelling, and the noun began to mean a dug shaft as well as a spring.
items.cn: 在中古英语中两种形式拼写趋同，名词也从泉水的意思扩展到人工挖成的井。

items.en: Deeper drilling brought the sense of an oil well, and the water picture stayed as a metaphor for abundance.
items.cn: 更深的钻探带来了油井之义，而水的形象则作为丰足的比喻保留下来。

items.en: The old adverb survives in fixed phrases such as do well, get well and as well as.
items.cn: 古老的副词在 do well、get well、as well as 等固定短语中保存下来。

note.en: The first group gathers words that share the shape of a hole or its mouth, the second the words for a source and for being in good condition.
note.cn: 第一组收与洞口、井口形体相关的词，第二组收表示来源与良好状态的说法。

entries.definition: An opening in the ground, dug or worn by use.
A large dug hollow, often for storing or trapping.
Water that rises by itself out of the ground.
The long straight passage of a well or a mine.
The place from which something comes, abstract as well as physical.
Free from illness, the adjective that matches being well.
In the right or expected way, as the adverb of doing something well.
A short opening word that softens the start of a remark, like a spoken well.

normalIntro.en: Two different words, a water hole and an old adverb, were written the same way, so the entry has to keep both pictures in mind.
normalIntro.cn: 一个水井名词和一个古老副词被写成了同一个形状，所以这个词条要同时记住两幅画面。

normal.en: See the w, mirrored as the walls of a round shaft, and the o, the mouth at the top.
normal.cn: 想字母 w 像圆井壁的两侧，字母 o 像井口。

normal.en: Water wells are dug; oil wells are drilled, but both are vertical tubes into the dark.
normal.cn: 水井是挖的，油井是钻的，但两者都是伸进黑暗里的竖管。

normal.en: A well of stories is the same picture with the water turned into words.
normal.cn: 「故事之井」是同一幅画面，只是水换成了语言。

normal.en: Well as an adverb hides in do well, get well and as well as.
normal.cn: 作副词的 well 藏在 do well、get well 和 as well as 里。

normal.en: At the start of a sentence it is only a soft noise that buys a second.
normal.cn: 放在句首时，它只是一个买来一秒钟的软声音。

abstract.en: Feel the cold air rising out of a stone mouth.
abstract.cn: 感受凉气从石头做的嘴里往上冒。

abstract.en: Hear a bucket rope creak and then stop.
abstract.cn: 听井绳吱呀作响，然后停住。

abstract.en: Picture a level of water that never moves though it is drawn from daily.
abstract.cn: 想一个天天被打水却始终不动的水面。

examples.en: The villagers still wash clothes beside the well.
examples.cn: 村民仍然在井边洗衣服。

examples.en: She did well in the exam without much preparation.
examples.cn: 她没怎么复习，考试却考得很好。

examples.en: Well, we can talk about it again tomorrow.
examples.cn: 嗯，我们明天可以再谈这件事。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂哦」——站在井边往下喂一声，回声从井底慢慢升上来。

root: 古英语 wiell（泉、涌出）与副词 wel（良好地）在中古英语时期拼写成形，成为同一个 well；另有 adj. good 的副词比较级 better、best。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts at a hole that gives water, widens to any shaft into the ground, becomes a picture of endless supply, and finally covers the old adverb of good and its health sense.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从出水的洞开始，扩大到任何伸入地下的竖井，再成为取之不尽的比喻，最后还覆盖了 good 的副词及健康之义。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone mouth in the ground with a rope hanging into it.
core.cn: 核心意象：地面上一张石头的嘴，一根绳子垂进去。

branches.en: The village branch: a bucket lifted from cold water.
branches.cn: 村庄分支：从冷水里提起的木桶。

branches.en: The industrial branch: three oil wells shut down.
branches.cn: 工业分支：关停的三口油井。

branches.en: The figurative branch: letters as a well of stories.
branches.cn: 比喻分支：作为故事之井的来信。

branches.en: The adverb branch: singing well and the pause word well.
branches.cn: 副词分支：唱得好，以及开口时的「嗯」。

branches.en: The health branch: not well, so staying at home.
branches.cn: 健康分支：身体不好，于是待在家里。

intro.en: Well is a whole Old English word rather than a derived form, but it joins freely in compounds such as wellness and wellhead, and in set phrases with the old adverb.
intro.cn: well 是完整的古英语词而非派生词，但它能自由参与 wellness、wellhead 这类复合词，也与古老副词构成固定短语。

latinIntro.en: The word is native Germanic, so there is no Latin source behind it; the Latin entries below are only cognate forms of the same family.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词是本土日耳曼词，背后没有拉丁语来源；下面的拉丁条目只是同一词族的同源形式。

items.meaning: a spring, a source of water
items.example: It is the plain noun we still use.
items.exampleCN: 这就是我们仍在使用的朴素名词。

items.example: It is the earliest recorded shape.
items.exampleCN: 它是最早有记录的词形。
它构成 wellhead 与 wellspring。

items.example: It gives the mouth of a well.
It gives a source that never runs dry.
items.exampleCN: 它给出一个永不干涸的源头。

items.example: The adverb survives here in a fixed frame.
items.exampleCN: 副词在这里以固定框架保存下来。

items.example: The old adverb keeps an irregular comparative.
items.exampleCN: 这个古老副词保留了不规则比较级。

definition_zh: 西；西方；西边；西部地区
definition_en: the direction where the sun goes down, and the part of a place or of the world that lies in that direction
core_image: 太阳沉到地平线后面，天边烧成一条橘红色的带子
scene: 傍晚站在田埂上，太阳正往山脊后面掉，整片天从橘红慢慢变紫。The sun sets in the west, so the kitchen windows glow every evening.
sceneCN: 这里 west 是「西」（第 1 个义项：太阳落下的方向）；句意为太阳从西边落下，所以每天傍晚厨房的窗子都会发亮。夕阳沉到地平线后的那条橘红色带子就是这个词的印象。

collocations.zh: 到西部去（尤指美国西部）

senses.title: The direction of the setting sun
senses.definition: the direction on the compass where the sun appears to go down, opposite to the east
senses.definitionCN: 指南针上太阳似乎落下的方向，与东相对
senses.example: The sun sets in the west, so the kitchen windows glow every evening.
senses.exampleCN: 太阳从西边落下，所以每天傍晚厨房的窗户都会发亮。
senses.why: All the Germanic languages tie this word to the evening side of the sky, so the direction itself is the base sense.
senses.whyCN: 所有日耳曼语言都把这个词与天空的黄昏一侧相绑，所以「方向」本身就是最基本的意思。

senses.title: The western part of a place
senses.definition: the area of a country, town or region that lies towards the west
senses.definitionCN: 一个国家、城镇或地区中靠西的那一部分
senses.example: Heavy rain is expected in the west of the province tonight.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚这个省的西部预计有大雨。
senses.why: Once a direction is fixed, the land lying in it takes the same name without any added ending.
senses.whyCN: 方向一旦固定，位于该方向上的土地就直接沿用同一个名字，不加任何词尾。

senses.title: The western countries
senses.definition: a loose name for Europe and North America, especially in historical and political writing
senses.definitionCN: 对欧洲与北美的笼统称呼，多用于历史与政治叙述
senses.example: Coffee reached the West through merchants in the seventeenth century.
senses.exampleCN: 咖啡在十七世纪经商人之手传到西方。
senses.why: The word stopped pointing at compasses and started naming a cultural block, drawn from maps with Europe on the left.
senses.whyCN: 这个词不再指罗盘，而是指一个文化板块，这源于欧洲被画在地图左方。

senses.title: Towards the west
senses.definition: in the adverb use, moving or facing in the western direction
senses.definitionCN: 副词用法，表示朝西移动或朝向西方
senses.example: They drove west until the road ran out at the sea.
senses.exampleCN: 他们一路向西开，直到路在海边断掉。
senses.why: English often uses a bare direction word as an adverb, so west does the work that westward does more formally.
senses.whyCN: 英语常把方向词直接当副词用，所以 west 承担了 westward 更正式地承担的工作。

intro.en: West descends from Old English west, from a Germanic base that named the evening side of the sky.
intro.cn: west 源自古英语 west，其日耳曼语词根指的是天空的黄昏一侧。

items.en: The common Germanic root carried the idea of evening and downward, so the direction was the place of the fading light.
items.cn: 共同的日耳曼词根带有「傍晚、向下」之意，因此这个方向就是光线消退之处。

items.en: Old English west was used both for the compass point and for the lands lying that way.
items.cn: 古英语 west 既指罗盘方位，也指位于该方向的土地。

items.en: The related adjective westan and the adverb westan gave English its fixed phrases for the setting sun.
items.cn: 相关的形容词与副词形式为英语留下了关于日落方向的固定说法。

items.en: The form settled as west, and compounds such as westwind and westland appeared in writing.
items.cn: 词形固定为 west，westwind、westland 等复合词也出现在文字中。

items.en: Empire and trade turned the compass point into a name for whole regions and cultures.
items.cn: 帝国与贸易把这个方位词变成了对整个地区与文化的称呼。

note.en: The first group gathers the other compass points, the second the words about western lands and movement that way.
note.cn: 第一组收其他方位词，第二组收表示西部土地与向西移动的说法。

entries.definition: The direction of sunrise, the opposite of west.
The direction to the left when one faces sunrise.
The direction to the right when one faces sunrise.
Towards the west, as a direction of travel.
The daily moment when the sun goes below the horizon.
A formal old name for the west, from the Latin word for falling.
A person who comes from the West, used in cultural talk.

normalIntro.en: The word is tied to the evening sky, so every picture of it should contain low light and a long shadow pointing the other way.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词与傍晚的天空相连，所以凡是想起它，都该带上一片低斜的光和一条指反方向的影子。

normal.en: West begins with the same sound as wet dusk air after rain.
normal.cn: west 的开头音与雨后傍晚潮湿空气的触感一样，都是 w 起头。

normal.en: The sun never says west; it just disappears there.
normal.cn: 太阳从不说「西」，它只是在那边消失。

normal.en: Maps put west on the left, the side where the page ends.
normal.cn: 地图把西放在左边，也就是纸页结束的那一侧。

normal.en: West Africa, West Lake, the West End: the same word is used as a label.
normal.cn: 西非、西湖、伦敦西区：同一个词被当作标签使用。

normal.en: Going west is going towards the light going down.
normal.cn: 向西走，就是朝着光落下的方向走。

abstract.en: Feel the last warmth on one cheek.
abstract.cn: 感觉最后一缕暖意贴在一边脸上。

abstract.en: See a shadow stretched longer than the person who casts it.
abstract.cn: 看见影子被拉得比投下它的人还长。

abstract.en: Hear the day quietly switching off.
abstract.cn: 听白昼悄悄关上开关。

examples.en: The wind blew from the west all night.
examples.cn: 风整夜都从西边吹来。

examples.en: Their farm lies to the west of the river.
examples.cn: 他们的农场位于河的西边。

examples.en: After the meeting he walked west along the main street.
examples.cn: 会议结束后，他沿着大街向西走去。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂斯特」——喂，斯特先生，太阳在那边落下去了，你往那边走就是西。

root: 日耳曼语词根（黄昏、向下）→ 古英语 west（西方）→ 中古英语 west → 现代英语 west；同族有 western、westward。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as the compass point of sunset, then covers the land in that direction, the cultural block called the West, and finally the bare adverb of going that way.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从日落方位的罗盘点出发，进而指该方向上的土地、被称为「西方」的文化板块，最后还承担了朝那边走的副词用法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an orange band of light sinking behind a ridge.
core.cn: 核心意象：山脊后面一条下沉的橘色光带。

branches.en: The compass branch: the sun sets in the west.
branches.cn: 方位分支：太阳从西边落下。

branches.en: The regional branch: rain in the west of the province.
branches.cn: 地区分支：省的西部有雨。

branches.en: The cultural branch: coffee reached the West.
branches.cn: 文化分支：咖啡传到西方。

branches.en: The movement branch: driving west to the sea.
branches.cn: 移动分支：一路向西开到海边。

branches.en: The naming branch: West Africa and the west wind, all built on the point itself.
branches.cn: 命名分支：西非与西风，都直接建立在方位点之上。

intro.en: West is a free Germanic root, and its family is built with the endings -ern, -ward and -most rather than with prefixes.
intro.cn: west 是自由使用的日耳曼语词根，其词族靠 -ern、-ward、-most 等词尾扩展，而不用前缀。

latinIntro.en: The Latin word for west was occidens, the falling, a participle of occidere, to go down, which is also the source of occident.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表「西」的词是 occidens（落下），源自 occidere（下去）的分词，也是 occident 的来源。

items.example: It works as noun, adjective and adverb.
items.exampleCN: 它可作名词、形容词与副词。

items.example: It is one of the oldest compounds.
items.exampleCN: 它是最古老的复合词之一。

items.example: A capital letter marks the cultural sense.
items.exampleCN: 大写字母标示出文化义。

items.example: The plural of the directional adverb.
items.exampleCN: 方向副词加 s 的变体。

definition_zh: 西方的；西部的；（Western）西方国家的；名词：西部片
definition_en: in or from the west, or belonging to Europe and North America
core_image: 太阳落到地图左半边，那边是西，人和风都从那一侧来
scene: 傍晚太阳压在地平线上，整片天烧成橙色。They drove west along the coast road until the light failed.
sceneCN: 这里 west 是「西方、西面」（第 1 个义项：太阳落下的方向）；句意为他们沿滨海公路向西开，直到天光消失。

pos.zh: 形容词：西方的、西部的；西方国家（尤指欧美）的
名词：西部影片、西部小说（常大写 Western）

derivatives.zh: 词根本身，义为「西、西方；西部的」
加 -er 构成，义为「西方人；西方居民」
加最高级后缀构成，义为「最西端的」
加 -ward 构成，义为「向西的」

senses.title: In or from the west
senses.titleCN: 西方的：位于或来自西边的
senses.definition: situated in the west, or coming from the west
senses.definitionCN: 位于西侧，或来自西边的
senses.example: The western half of the island is wetter and greener.
senses.exampleCN: 岛上的西半部更潮湿、更青绿。
senses.why: The adjective simply takes the compass word west and adds -ern, as in eastern and southern: it names a position on the compass.
senses.whyCN: 这个形容词只是把方位词 west 加上后缀 -ern（如同 eastern、southern），表示罗盘上的位置。

senses.title: Belonging to the West
senses.titleCN: 西方国家的：属于欧美的
senses.definition: belonging to Europe and North America, especially their shared culture and institutions
senses.definitionCN: 属于欧洲与北美，尤指其共同文化与制度
senses.example: She studied western philosophy before turning to Chinese classics.
senses.exampleCN: 她先学西方哲学，后来转向中国典籍。
senses.why: Here the word is capitalised in use and means a civilisation, not a compass point: the West as a cultural region.
senses.whyCN: 这里该词实际常大写，指一种文明而非罗盘方向：作为文化区域的「西方」。

senses.title: Facing west
senses.definition: facing towards the west
senses.definitionCN: 面朝西边
senses.example: The western windows catch the last of the sun.
senses.exampleCN: 朝西的窗户能接住最后的阳光。
senses.why: A building or room is described by the side the compass says it faces; the meaning turns from origin to orientation.
senses.whyCN: 建筑物或房间按罗盘所指的朝向描述；词义从「来源」转为「朝向」。

senses.title: The western film
senses.titleCN: 西部片：以美国西部为背景的影片
senses.definition: as a noun, a film or novel about cowboys and settlers in the American West
senses.definitionCN: 名词用法，指以美国西部牛仔与拓荒者为题材的电影或小说
senses.example: He watched an old western on Sunday afternoons.
senses.exampleCN: 他周日下午看一部老西部片。
senses.why: The adjective, used as a noun, names a genre: the stories set in the American West, and the word for the direction became the word for that world.
senses.whyCN: 形容词用作名词就指一种类型：以美国西部为背景的故事，于是表示方向的词成了那个世界的名字。

senses.title: Western as opposed to eastern practice
senses.titleCN: 西式的：与东方做法相对的
senses.definition: used to mark the European or American form of something, as in western medicine
senses.definitionCN: 用于标示某事物欧美式的形态，如 western medicine（西医）
senses.example: The clinic combines western medicine with herbal treatment.
senses.exampleCN: 这家诊所把西医与草药治疗结合起来。
senses.why: In compounds the word becomes a label of method: it says which tradition a practice comes from, not where it is done.
senses.whyCN: 在复合词中这个词成了方法的标签：它说明某种做法源自哪种传统，而非在哪里做。

intro.en: Western is an Old English adjective formed on west, the direction of sunset, with the -ern ending seen in eastern and southern.
intro.cn: western 是古英语形容词，由表示日落方向的 west 加后缀 -ern 构成，与 eastern、southern 同类。

items.en: Westerne meant 'western, lying to the west', built on west with the adjective ending -erne.
items.cn: 古英语 westerne 意为「西方的、在西边的」，由 west 加形容词词尾 -erne 构成。

items.en: The base west is a Germanic word for the direction of sunset, so the adjective belongs to the oldest layer of the vocabulary.
items.cn: 本词 west 是日耳曼语中表示日落方向的词，因此该形容词属于最古老的词汇层。

items.en: West itself named the direction of the setting sun, a word shared by the Germanic languages.
items.cn: west 本身指日落的方位，是日耳曼诸语言共有的词。

items.en: The spelling became western, and the word was used for winds, shores and parts of a country.
items.cn: 拼写演变为 western，用于西风、西岸以及一国的西半部。

items.en: From the sixteenth century it also named the lands of Europe and America as a group, and later the cowboy film.
items.cn: 自十六世纪起，它也用来统称欧美诸国，后来又指牛仔电影。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers other compass adjectives and the family of west; the near-meaning group gathers words for the West as a region.
note.cn: 形近组收其他方位形容词与 west 一族词；近义组收表示「西方」这一区域的词。

entries.definition: The matching adjective for the east.
entries.definitionCN: 同类形容词，义为「东方的」。

entries.definition: The matching adjective for the north.
entries.definitionCN: 同类形容词，义为「北方的」。

entries.definition: Towards the west; an adverb, not an adjective of place.
A person from the West; the derived noun.
The direction itself; the noun behind the adjective.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「西」，是形容词背后的方位词。

entries.definition: A formal word for western, from Latin for the setting sun.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语，义为「西方的」，源自拉丁语「日落」。

entries.definition: Narrower: of Europe only, without America.
entries.definitionCN: 名词或形容词，范围更窄，只指欧洲。

entries.definition: Travelling towards the west, said of traffic.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「向西行驶的」，多用于交通。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old English root west and the phrases the word actually appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子使用真实的古英语词根 west，以及这个词实际出现的短语。

normal.en: West is where the sun sets; western is the side it sets on.
normal.cn: west 是太阳落下的地方；western 就是日落的那一侧。

normal.en: The -ern ending turns a compass point into an adjective, as in eastern and southern.
normal.cn: 后缀 -ern 把方位词变成形容词，如 eastern、southern。

normal.en: Capitalised, the West means Europe and North America as a culture.
normal.cn: 大写时 the West 指作为文化整体的欧美。

normal.en: A western is a film about the American West.
normal.cn: a western 指一部关于美国西部的电影。

normal.en: Western medicine stands opposite Chinese medicine in the phrase.
normal.cn: western medicine 在说法上与中医相对。

abstract.en: Stand facing the sunset: everything on your left hand is west.
abstract.cn: 面朝日落站着：左手边的一切都是西。

abstract.en: The word moves from a direction to a civilisation without changing shape.
abstract.cn: 这个词从一个方向滑向一种文明，形态却不变。

abstract.en: Every map makes its own centre, so western is always western relative to a chosen standpoint.
abstract.cn: 每张地图都有自己的中心，所以 western 总是相对于某个既定位置而言的西方。

examples.en: Western Australia is the largest state in the country.
examples.cn: 西澳大利亚是这个国家最大的州。

examples.en: The museum has a fine collection of western paintings.
examples.cn: 这家博物馆收藏了不少西方绘画佳作。

examples.en: They spent the evening watching an old western.
examples.cn: 他们整个晚上都在看一部老西部片。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「歪死疼」——往西走的人被风吹得歪得要死要疼：西边的

root: 古英语 west「日落的方向、西」→ westerne「西边的」→ 英语 western；同族词有 west、westerner、westernmost、westward。

sensesIntro.en: Five senses of western run from a compass position to a civilisation: lying to the west, belonging to the West, facing west, a cowboy film, and a label for method.
sensesIntro.cn: western 的五个义项从方位走到文明：位于西边、属于欧美、朝西、西部片，以及标示方法的西式。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the sun going down on the left half of the map.
core.cn: 核心意象：太阳落到地图左半边。

branches.en: THE POSITION: the western half of a place.
branches.cn: 位置线：一个地方的西半部。

branches.en: THE CIVILISATION: Europe and America as the West.
branches.cn: 文明线：作为「西方」的欧美。

branches.en: THE ORIENTATION: western windows take the last sun.
branches.cn: 朝向线：朝西的窗户接住最后的阳光。

branches.en: THE GENRE: a western is a film of the American West.
branches.cn: 类型线：a western 是美国西部的影片。

branches.en: THE METHOD: western medicine names a tradition.
branches.cn: 方法线：western medicine 指一种传统。

intro.en: Western is a native English adjective; the -ern ending and the -er of westerner do the work.
intro.cn: western 是英语本族形容词；起作用的是后缀 -ern 与 westerner 中的 -er。

latinIntro.en: West is Germanic, not Latin; only the scholarly doublet occidental comes through Latin occidens, the setting sun.
latinIntro.cn: west 属日耳曼语而非拉丁语；只有学究气的同义词 occidental 来自拉丁语 occidens「日落」。

items.example: It is the base noun of the family.
It forms western, as in eastern.
It gives occidental, the Latin-side word for western.
items.exampleCN: 它生出 occidental，即拉丁系的「西方」。

definition_zh: 什么；（用于感叹句）多么；所…的事物
definition_en: used to ask about a thing, to express surprise or to introduce a noun clause about a thing
core_image: 一个人歪着头，把手一摊，眉头上写着一个问号
scene: 老人把一袋东西递过来，你歪头摊手，嘴里只吐出这个短词。You did not say what the price was, so I guessed.
sceneCN: 这里 what 是疑问词「什么」（第 1 个义项：询问事物）；句意为你没说价钱是多少，所以我猜了一下。歪头摊手、眉头上一个问号的动作就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: The thing asked about
senses.definition: used at the start of a question to ask which thing or kind of thing
senses.definitionCN: 用在问句开头，询问是哪一样事物或哪一类事物
senses.example: What did she say at the meeting?
senses.exampleCN: 她在会上说了什么？
senses.why: The oldest use in English is the interrogative particle, and all the other meanings of the word grow out of this asking function.
senses.whyCN: 英语中最早的用法就是疑问词，这个词其余含义都由这种提问功能长出。

senses.title: The thing that
senses.titleCN: 所…的事物（引导名词从句）
senses.definition: used to introduce a clause naming the thing that is talked about or done
senses.definitionCN: 引导一个名词性从句，指出所谈到或所做的那件事
senses.example: You did not say what the price was, so I guessed.
senses.exampleCN: 你没说价钱是多少，所以我猜了一下。
senses.why: A question inside a longer sentence keeps its shape but loses its question mark, so what also links two clauses.
senses.whyCN: 嵌在长句中的问句保留形状却失去问号，于是 what 也承担了连接两个分句的作用。

senses.title: In an exclamation
senses.definition: used before a noun phrase to express strong feeling about a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词短语前，对人或事表达强烈感情
senses.example: What a wonderful idea that is!
senses.exampleCN: 这真是个绝妙的主意！
senses.why: Surprise is a question that answers itself, so the interrogative word became an exclamation without any change of form.
senses.whyCN: 惊讶是一个自问自答的问句，于是这个疑问词不加变化就成了感叹词。

senses.title: An opinion or a remark
senses.definition: in informal questions such as what do you think of, used to ask for an opinion
senses.definitionCN: 在 what do you think of 等口语问句中，用来征求对某事的看法
senses.example: What do you make of his plan?
senses.exampleCN: 你看他这个计划怎么样？
senses.why: Asking for an opinion is still asking what something is, viewed through a person's judgement.
senses.whyCN: 征求看法仍是询问某物是什么，只是透过某人的判断来看。

senses.title: A tired answer of surprise
senses.definition: a short exclamation used alone to show that one has not heard or cannot believe something
senses.definitionCN: 单独使用，表示没听清或难以相信某事
senses.example: What? They cancelled the trip again?
senses.exampleCN: 什么？他们把旅行又取消了？
senses.why: When the whole question is cut down to one syllable, only this half of it is left.
senses.whyCN: 整个问句被砍成一个音节时，只剩下了它的这一半。

intro.en: What is the Old English neuter of hwā, the word that also gave who, and it has kept the same function for over a thousand years.
intro.cn: what 是古英语 hwā（也产生了 who）的中性形式，一千多年来功能未变。

items.en: The Germanic interrogative stem hwa- carried an initial hw sound that later became the wh of English.
items.cn: 日耳曼语的疑问词干 hwa- 带有一个 hw 音，后来变成英语的 wh。

items.en: Hwæt was the general word for what, working as pronoun and as the opener of exclamations.
items.cn: hwæt 是指「什么」的通称，既作代词，也作感叹句的开头。

items.en: The letter sequence settled as what, and the word began to link clauses as a relative pronoun.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 what，这个词也开始作为关系代词连接从句。

items.en: What and which divided the work between open questions and narrowed choices.
items.cn: what 与 which 分工，一个用于开放提问，一个用于缩小选择范围。

items.en: Spoken English shortened it further into answers such as what for, what if and the flat what of surprise.
items.cn: 口语英语进一步把它缩短成 what for、what if 以及表示惊讶的短促 what。

note.en: The first group collects the other English question words, the second the words that ask about things and choices.
note.cn: 第一组收英语其他的疑问词，第二组收询问事物与选择的相关说法。

entries.definition: Asks about one member out of a known set.
entries.definitionCN: 哪一个（在已知的范围内）

entries.definition: The same family, but asks about people.
The same family, but asks about time.
Also links clauses about things, but without a question inside.
entries.definitionCN: 也可连接名词从句，但内部不含疑问

entries.definition: What, widened to any thing at all.
Asks about manner where what asks about a thing.
A polite way to say that one has not heard, the job of a spoken what.

normalIntro.en: The whole family of wh question words starts with a rounded mouth, and what is the widest of them because it asks about anything.
normalIntro.cn: 整个 wh 疑问词族都以一个圆唇音开头，而 what 最宽，因为它问的是任何东西。

normal.en: What, where, when, which, who: the same wh, five different things to ask about.
normal.cn: what、where、when、which、who：同一个 wh，问五种不同的事。

normal.en: What asks the open question; which asks inside a list.
normal.cn: what 问开放式问题，which 在名单里问。

normal.en: Put an exclamation mark after it and it becomes praise or shock.
normal.cn: 在它后面加个感叹号，它就成了赞美或震惊。

normal.en: What plus ever makes the category total; what plus so makes it smaller.
normal.cn: what 加 ever 表示全部范畴，what 加 so 表示更少。

normal.en: Said alone and flat, it means one has not heard a word.
normal.cn: 单独平平地说出来，它表示一个字也没听清。

abstract.en: Feel the chin drop when the mouth opens on the vowel.
abstract.cn: 感受发元音时下巴往下掉。

abstract.en: See an empty box held up for someone to fill in.
abstract.cn: 看一只空盒子被举起来，等人填进去。

abstract.en: Hear the rising tone of a question in one syllable.
abstract.cn: 听一个音节里升起的问句语调。

examples.en: What do you want for lunch?
examples.cn: 你午饭想吃什么？

examples.en: Tell me what happened after I left.
examples.cn: 告诉我我走之后发生了什么。

examples.en: What a beautiful morning it is!
examples.cn: 多么美好的早晨啊！

dict_mnemonic.text: 「沃特」——沃特歪着头问：你说的那个到底是啥？

root: 古英语 hwæt（什么，即 hwā 的中性）→ 中古英语 what；同族有 who、which、when、whatsoever。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as a plain question about a thing, then links clauses, then breaks out into exclamations, then asks for an opinion, and finally stands alone as a one-syllable what of surprise.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先是对事物的单纯提问，继而连接从句，再爆成感叹，随后用来征求意见，最后单独站成一个表示惊讶的短词。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tilted head and an open hand, waiting for a thing to be named.
core.cn: 核心意象：歪着头、摊开手，等某样东西被说出来。

branches.en: The question branch: what did she say at the meeting.
branches.cn: 提问分支：她在会上说了什么。

branches.en: The linking branch: what the price was.
branches.cn: 连接分支：价钱是多少。

branches.en: The exclamation branch: what a wonderful idea.
branches.cn: 感叹分支：多么绝妙的主意。

branches.en: The opinion branch: what do you make of it.
branches.cn: 看法分支：你看这件事怎么样。

branches.en: The deaf branch: a flat what when a word was missed.
branches.cn: 没听清分支：漏听时平平的一声 what。

intro.en: What is a free stem of Germanic origin, and it builds a small family with ever, so and some rather than with prefixes.
intro.cn: what 是日耳曼语来源的自由词干，它的词族靠 ever、so、some 构成，而不是靠前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin had the interrogative pronominal stem quo-, which underlies quid, what; the entries below are the borrowed roots, not ancestors of what.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语有疑问词干 quo-，由此构成 quid（什么）；下面的条目是借入词根，并非 what 的祖先。

definition_zh: 轮子；车轮；方向盘；推动；（鸟）盘旋
definition_en: a round object that turns on an axle, used under vehicles and machines, and by extension the act of turning or of pushing something along
core_image: 一只木轮压过土路，辐条在眼前飞快地转成一圈影子
scene: 牛车碾过土路，木轮转得辐条糊成一圈。The back wheel of my bike came off on the hill.
sceneCN: 这里 wheel 是「轮子」（第 1 个义项：绕轴转动的圆形部件）；句意为我自行车的后轮在山坡上掉了。木轮压过土路、辐条糊成一圈影子，就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 轮子；车轮；方向盘；轮状物

senses.title: The turning ring under a vehicle
senses.definition: a circular object that turns about an axle and lets a vehicle or machine move
senses.definitionCN: 绕轴旋转的圆形物体，使车辆或机器得以移动
senses.example: The back wheel of my bike came off on the hill.
senses.exampleCN: 我自行车的后轮在山坡上掉了。
senses.why: This is the base sense of the word, and every other meaning either names a similar round thing or describes turning.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最基本的意思，其余含义若不是指类似的圆形物，就是描述转动。

senses.title: The thing you hold in a car
senses.definition: the circular handle in a vehicle by which the driver turns it
senses.definitionCN: 车辆中供驾驶员转向的圆形把手
senses.example: She never let anyone else take the wheel on long trips.
senses.exampleCN: 长途旅行时她从不让别人握方向盘。
senses.why: A steering wheel is just a wheel mounted on a column, and the part kept the name of the whole circle.
senses.whyCN: 方向盘不过是一枚装在转向柱上的轮，这个部件就沿用了整个圆的名称。

senses.title: A round flat object
senses.definition: something shaped like a wheel, especially a round food such as a cheese
senses.definitionCN: 形状像轮子的东西，尤指一轮圆形的食物如干酪
senses.example: They cut a whole wheel of cheese into thin slices.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把一整轮干酪切成薄片。
senses.why: The shape is the whole point, so the word simply moves onto anything round and flat with a rim.
senses.whyCN: 形状就是全部要点，于是这个词直接移用到任何圆而平、带边的东西上。

senses.title: To push something on wheels
senses.definition: to move something along on wheels, or to push a cart or trolley
senses.definitionCN: 用轮子把某物移走，或推手推车
senses.example: They wheeled the bed into the next room.
senses.exampleCN: 他们把床推进了隔壁的房间。
senses.why: Once the object is named, the same sound becomes the action of moving on it, as with any tool in English.
senses.whyCN: 物件被命名之后，同一个声音又成了靠它移动的动作，英语中任何工具词都可如此。

senses.title: To circle in the air
senses.definition: used of birds or aircraft turning in wide circles without moving away
senses.definitionCN: 用于鸟或飞机在空中绕大圈而不离开
senses.example: Gulls wheeled above the fishing boats all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 海鸥整下午都在渔船上方盘旋。
senses.why: A circle in the sky copies the motion of a wheel, so the verb turns the wheel picture ninety degrees up.
senses.whyCN: 天空中的圆圈拷贝了轮子的运动，于是这个动词把轮子的画面竖了起来。

intro.en: Wheel comes from Old English hwēol, from a Germanic root meaning to turn, and the same turning root lies behind the Latin words for circle and column.
intro.cn: wheel 源自古英语 hwēol，其日耳曼语词根意为「转动」，同一个转动的词根也藏在拉丁语的圆与轮子诸词中。

items.en: The root meant to turn or to roll, so the object was named for what it does rather than what it looks like.
items.cn: 这个词根意为转动或滚动，所以物件是按它做的事、而不是按样子命名的。

items.en: Hwēol appears in early riddles and poems about wagons and the sun moving across the sky.
items.cn: hwēol 出现在早期关于货车与日轮横空的谜语和诗歌中。

items.en: The spelling moved from hwēol to wheel, and the word was applied to the wheel of a ship and later of a cart.
items.cn: 拼写从 hwēol 变为 wheel，此词先用于船的舵轮，后用于马车的轮。

items.en: Roads and engines turned wheel into a verb for pushing carts and for birds circling in the air.
items.cn: 道路与引擎让 wheel 成为动词，表示推车以及鸟在空中盘旋。

items.en: The phrase behind the wheel marks the steering wheel, and wheels of industry carries the turning picture into economics.
items.cn: behind the wheel 标记着方向盘，wheels of industry 则把转动的画面带入经济。

note.en: The first group gathers round things or words spelled like wheel, the second the words for turning and for a driving position.
note.cn: 第一组收圆的东西或与 wheel 拼写相近的词，第二组收表示转动与驾驶位置的说法。

entries.definition: The sea animal, with a different vowel.
To become well again, almost the same sound.
To spin fast, the nearest cousin in meaning.
The bar a wheel turns on.
The rubber ring fitted around a wheel.
The full name of the car part.
The shape a wheel copies, and the path of a wheeling bird.
The wheeled thing one wheels around a shop.

normalIntro.en: The word looks like a wheel on the page: a round o held between two uprights, and the doubled e is the two hubs.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词在纸面上就像一个轮子：两个竖笔夹住一个圆 o，双写 e 像两个轮毂。

normal.en: Wheel and wh-eel: an eel bent into a circle is a wheel.
normal.cn: wheel 里有 eel（鳗鱼）：一条鳗鱼弯成圈，就成了轮子。

normal.en: Behind the wheel is a place, not a thing: the driver's seat.
normal.cn: behind the wheel 是位置而不是物件：驾驶者的座位。

normal.en: A wheel of cheese borrows the shape and leaves the road behind.
normal.cn: a wheel of cheese 借走了形状，把马路留在了后面。

normal.en: Wheeling a bed is the same action as turning a wheel, without the round object.
normal.cn: 把床推走与转轮是同一个动作，只是没有那个圆东西。

normal.en: Gulls wheel because a circle in the air is a wheel seen from below.
normal.cn: 海鸥盘旋，因为空中的圆圈是从下方看到的轮子。

abstract.en: Feel the road under a wooden rim.
abstract.cn: 感觉木轮边下的路面。

abstract.en: See spokes blur into one grey disc.
abstract.cn: 看辐条糊成一张灰色圆盘。

abstract.en: Hear a cart stop with a single knock.
abstract.cn: 听马车咯噔一声停住。

examples.en: One wheel of the cart was stuck in the mud.
examples.cn: 马车的一只轮子陷进了泥里。

examples.en: He fell asleep at the wheel and woke up at the lights.
examples.cn: 他开车时睡着了，到红绿灯才醒来。

examples.en: Nurses wheeled the patient down the corridor.
examples.cn: 护士把病人推过走廊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威尔」——威尔推着车走，轮子吱吱响，一路滚到村口。

root: 日耳曼语词根（转动、滚动）→ 古英语 hwēol → 中古英语 wheel；同族有 whirl、wheelchair、wheelbarrow。

sensesIntro.en: The word names the turning ring first, then the steering ring, then any round slab, then the act of pushing on wheels, and finally the circling of a bird.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先指会转的圈，再指方向盘那个圈，然后指任何圆块，接着指用车推的动作，最后指鸟的盘旋。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden rim turning with its spokes blurred.
core.cn: 核心意象：一只木轮转得辐条发糊。

branches.en: The vehicle branch: a bike wheel coming off on the hill.
branches.cn: 车辆分支：山坡上掉落的自行车轮。

branches.en: The driving branch: never letting anyone take the wheel.
branches.cn: 驾驶分支：从不让别人握方向盘。

branches.en: The shape branch: a wheel of cheese cut into slices.
branches.cn: 形状分支：切成片的一轮干酪。

branches.en: The action branch: wheeling a bed into the next room.
branches.cn: 动作分支：把床推进隔壁房间。

branches.en: The sky branch: gulls wheeling above the boats.
branches.cn: 天空分支：渔船上方盘旋的海鸥。

intro.en: Wheel is a whole Old English noun that also serves as a verb, and the family grows through -ing, -ed and compounds such as -chair and -barrow.
intro.cn: wheel 是完整的古英语名词，也能作动词，词族通过 -ing、-ed 及 -chair、-barrow 等复合成分扩展。

latinIntro.en: The Latin word for wheel, rota, also gave rotate and rotor, so the entries below are the borrowed cousins of the same object.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表轮的 rota 也产生了 rotate 与 rotor，所以下面的条目是同一物件的借入近亲。

items.example: It is both a noun and a verb.
items.exampleCN: 它既可作名词也可作动词。

items.example: It is the earliest recorded shape.
items.exampleCN: 它是最早有记录的词形。

items.example: The wheel keeps only half the name here.
items.exampleCN: 这里轮只保留了一半的名字。

items.example: It names a position rather than an object.

definition_zh: 什么时候；当…的时候；那时
definition_en: used to ask about the time of something, or to introduce the time at which a thing happens
core_image: 手指点在日历上某一个格子里
scene: 她翻着日历，指尖停在一格上抬头问：到底哪一天？Call me when the train arrives.
sceneCN: 这里 when 是「当…的时候」（第 2 个义项：引出某事发生的时间）；句意为火车到的时候给我打电话。手指点在日历某一格上，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: At what time
senses.definition: used at the start of a question to ask about the time of an event
senses.definitionCN: 用在问句开头，询问事件发生的时间
senses.example: When does the last bus leave?
senses.exampleCN: 末班车什么时候走？
senses.why: The interrogative use is the oldest function and gives the word its shape and its wh- sound.
senses.whyCN: 疑问用法是最古老的功能，也为这个词定下了形状和 wh- 的开头音。

senses.title: At the time that
senses.definition: used to join two clauses, marking the time at which the second happens
senses.definitionCN: 连接两个分句，标出后者发生的时间
senses.example: Call me when the train arrives.
senses.exampleCN: 火车到的时候给我打电话。
senses.why: The same word stopped asking and started pointing at a known time once the time was supplied by the other clause.
senses.whyCN: 一旦另一个分句给出了时间，这个词就不再提问，转而指向那个已知的时刻。

senses.title: The time at which
senses.definition: used after a time noun to introduce the clause that describes that time
senses.definitionCN: 用在时间名词之后，引出描述那个时间的从句
senses.example: I still remember the day when we first met.
senses.exampleCN: 我还记得我们初次见面的那一天。
senses.why: A day or a year is a time already named, so when only carries the meaning forward into the clause.
senses.whyCN: 「某一天」或「某一年」已经是点明的时间，于是 when 只需把这意思带进从句。

senses.title: Although, given that
senses.titleCN: （用于说明理由或让步）既然；而…却
senses.definition: used to introduce a fact that makes the main statement surprising or explains it
senses.definitionCN: 引出一个使主句显得出人意料或构成解释的事实
senses.example: Why buy a new coat when you have three?
senses.exampleCN: 你都有三件了，为什么还买新外套？
senses.why: The time link loosens into a condition, so the clause gives a reason or a contrast rather than a moment.
senses.whyCN: 时间上的连接松化为条件，于是从句给出的不再是时刻，而是理由或对照。

senses.title: And then, at that point
senses.definition: used at the end of a statement to name the moment something happened
senses.definitionCN: 用在陈述句末尾，指明某事发生的那个时刻
senses.example: We were about to leave when the phone rang.
senses.exampleCN: 我们正要出门，这时电话响了。
senses.why: A time word can sit at the end of a clause, where it works like a hinge to turn the story.
senses.whyCN: 时间词可以放在句末，在那里像合页一样把故事转过去。

intro.en: When comes from Old English hwænne, the interrogative adverb of time, built on the same hwa- stem as who and what.
intro.cn: when 源自古英语 hwænne，即表示时间的疑问副词，与 who、what 建立在同一个 hwa- 词干上。

items.en: The stem hwa- asked all the questions, and its time member kept a final n sound.
items.cn: 词干 hwa- 承担所有提问，其中问时间的那一支带有收尾的 n 音。

items.en: Hwænne was used both in direct questions and to link clauses about time.
items.cn: hwænne 既用于直接问句，也用于连接关于时间的从句。

items.en: The spelling settled as when, and the word began to follow nouns such as day and year.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 when，这个词开始跟在 day、year 等名词之后。

items.en: The relative use grew in prose, giving the day when and the year when.
items.cn: 关系用法在散文中增长，产生了 the day when 与 the year when。

items.en: Conversation added the looser reasons and contrasts of why buy it when you have three.
items.cn: 口语发展出更松散的理由与对照用法，如「你都有三件了，为什么还买」。

note.en: The first group gathers the other time words and question words, the second the words that link events in time.
note.cn: 第一组收其他时间词与疑问词，第二组收在时间上连接事件的说法。

entries.definition: The place version of the same stem.
At any time at all.
At that time, the answer side of when.
entries.definitionCN: 那时，是 when 的回答面

entries.definition: During the time that, a duration rather than a point.
entries.definitionCN: 当…期间，指时段而非时间点

entries.definition: The moment that, an emphatic version of the linking when.
After the time that, close to the reason use of when.
The thing that when asks about.

normalIntro.en: The word is short and pointed, like a finger on one square of a calendar.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词短而尖，就像一只手指点在日历的某一格上。

normal.en: When, where, why: the same wh, three questions about time, place and cause.
normal.cn: when、where、why：同一个 wh，分别问时间、地点与原因。

normal.en: The answer to when is then, and the two words differ by one consonant.
normal.cn: when 的答案是 then，两个词只差一个辅音。

normal.en: While lasts, when points: one covers a duration, the other a moment.
normal.cn: while 持续，when 指向：一个覆盖时段，一个标记瞬间。

normal.en: In the middle of a story, a sentence-ending when turns the corner.
normal.cn: 在叙事中间，句末的 when 就是一个转弯。

normal.en: After a negative or a comparison, when can even carry a reason.
normal.cn: 在否定或比较之后，when 甚至能带上理由的意味。

abstract.en: Feel one finger press a single date.
abstract.cn: 感觉一只手指压住某一个日期。

abstract.en: See two clauses joined at a single point.
abstract.cn: 看两个分句在某一点上接合。

abstract.en: Hear a phone ring exactly as the door opens.
abstract.cn: 听见门正打开时电话正好响起。

examples.en: When did you last see him?
examples.cn: 你最后一次见他是什么时候？

examples.en: She was reading when the lights went out.
examples.cn: 灯灭的时候她正在看书。

examples.en: Why wait when the answer is already clear?
examples.cn: 答案已经清楚了，为什么还要等？

dict_mnemonic.text: 「温」——温先生问：什么时候去温泉？指在日历上一格。

root: 古英语 hwænne（何时，hwa- 词干）→ 中古英语 when；同族有 where、why、whenever。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as the time question, then links a known time to a clause, then names that time after a noun, then loosens into reason, and finally sits at a sentence end to turn a story.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先问时间，再把已知时间与从句相连，随后在名词后指认那个时间，再松化为理由，最后坐在句末给故事转弯。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fingertip on one square of a calendar.
core.cn: 核心意象：指尖落在日历的一格上。

branches.en: The question branch: when does the last bus leave.
branches.cn: 提问分支：末班车什么时候开。

branches.en: The linking branch: call me when the train arrives.
branches.cn: 连接分支：火车到的时候打电话。

branches.en: The relative branch: the day when we first met.
branches.cn: 关系分支：我们初见的那一天。

branches.en: The reason branch: why buy a coat when you have three.
branches.cn: 理由分支：都有三件了还买外套做什么。

branches.en: The hinge branch: we were leaving when the phone rang.
branches.cn: 转折分支：我们正要走，电话响了。

intro.en: When is a free Germanic stem, so its family is built with ever and with the kindred words where and why rather than with prefixes.
intro.cn: when 是自由的日耳曼语词干，它的词族用 ever 以及 where、why 等同源词构成，而不是用前缀。

latinIntro.en: Latin asked the time with quando, which also gives the borrowed quando and the logic word quandary; entries below are parallels, not ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 quando 问时间，也由此借入 quando 与 quandary；下面条目是并行说法，并非祖源。

items.example: It works as adverb, conjunction and relative word.
items.exampleCN: 它可作副词、连词和关系词。

items.example: It forms whence in older English.
items.exampleCN: 它在旧英语中构成 whence。

items.example: It packs a time link into one word.
items.exampleCN: 它把时间关系压进一个词。

items.example: It shows when marking a condition.
items.exampleCN: 它显示 when 标记条件。

items.example: It narrows a topic rather than a time.
items.exampleCN: 它缩小的是话题而不是时间。

items.example: It is the sharp version of linking when.
items.exampleCN: 它是连接用法的锋利版本。

definition_zh: 在哪里；往哪里；在…的地方；在某一点上
definition_en: used to ask about a place, or to introduce the place in or to which something happens
core_image: 手指按在地图上的一个点，指甲下面露出一点颜色
scene: 两个人对着地图，有人用手指按住某一小块地方，抬头问。Do you know where the key is?
sceneCN: 这里 where 是「在哪里」（第 1 个义项：询问地点）；句意为你知不知道钥匙在哪儿？手指按在地图上那一点就是这个词的印象。

collocations.zh: 你从哪里来；你是哪儿人

senses.title: In or to what place
senses.definition: used to ask about a place or the direction of movement
senses.definitionCN: 询问地点或移动的方向
senses.example: Do you know where the key is?
senses.exampleCN: 你知不知道钥匙在哪儿？
senses.why: This is the base function of the word, and every other sense either points at a place or moves along it.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词最基本的功能，其余含义或指向某处，或沿某处移动。

senses.title: In the place that
senses.definition: used to introduce a clause naming a place, usually the place of the main action
senses.definitionCN: 引出一个指明地点的从句，通常是主句动作发生的地方
senses.example: Put the box where the children cannot reach it.
senses.exampleCN: 把箱子放在孩子够不到的地方。
senses.why: A question inside a sentence keeps its place meaning but loses its question mark.
senses.whyCN: 嵌在句中的问句保留地点含义，却失去了问号。

senses.title: The place at which
senses.definition: used after a place noun to introduce the description of that place
senses.definitionCN: 用在表示地点的名词后，引出对该地点的描述
senses.example: This is the village where she grew up.
senses.exampleCN: 这就是她长大的村子。
senses.why: Once the place is already named by a noun, where only carries it into the clause.
senses.whyCN: 地点一旦已由名词点明，where 只需把它带进从句。

senses.title: In the respect that
senses.definition: used in formal writing to point at a part or a respect rather than a physical place
senses.definitionCN: 用于正式文字，指向某一方面或某一环节而不是物理地点
senses.example: The plan has one fault where the cost is concerned.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划在花费方面有一个毛病。
senses.why: Place talk widens into abstract ground, so a subject or a paragraph can also be a where.
senses.whyCN: 地点的说法扩大到抽象的立足点，于是一个话题或一段文字也可以是一个 where。

intro.en: Where comes from Old English hwær, the place adverb built on the same hwa- stem as who, what and when.
intro.cn: where 源自古英语 hwær，是建立在 who、what、when 同一 hwa- 词干上的地点副词。

items.en: The stem hwa- had a place member whose sound ended in an r, and that r is all that distinguishes where from what.
items.cn: hwa- 词干有一支表地点，其音以 r 收尾，这个 r 就是 where 与 what 的全部差别。

items.en: Hwær asked about place in both questions and clauses, and its relatives hwider and hwæder covered motion.
items.cn: hwær 在问句与从句中问地点，其相关形式 hwider 与 hwæder 负责运动方向。

items.en: The spelling became where, and English also gained whence for from where.
items.cn: 拼写变为 where，英语另有 whence 表示「从何处」。

items.en: The relative use grew beside the question use, giving sentences like the house where we lived.
items.cn: 关系用法在疑问用法旁边成长，产生了 the house where we lived 这样的句子。

items.en: Formal prose extended the word to abstract points, as in where the cost is concerned.
items.cn: 正式文字把这个词扩展到抽象的点上，如 where the cost is concerned。

note.en: The first group gathers the other wh words and place words, the second the words for place and for direction of travel.
note.cn: 第一组收其他 wh 词与地点词，第二组收表示地点与行进方向的说法。

entries.definition: The time version of the same stem.
Whereas began as where plus so, and now contrasts clauses.
entries.definitionCN: whereas 本是 where 加 so，现在用于对比从句

entries.definition: Any place at all.
The past of be, which looks almost identical.
entries.definitionCN: be 的过去式，外形几乎一样

entries.definition: The thing that where asks about.
To what place, the old motion form, now literary.
entries.definitionCN: 往何处（旧用法，现多书面）

entries.definition: From what place, the old source form.
In a place not named, the vague answer to where.

normalIntro.en: Where has the r of a finger pointing, and everything in its family keeps that r.
normalIntro.cn: where 里有一个像用手指指的 r，词族里的词都保留着它。

normal.en: Where, here, there: the same -ere, ending in a place that is either asked or shown.
normal.cn: where、here、there：同样的 -ere，结尾或是问的地点，或是指出的地点。

normal.en: Wh- keeps the question; here and there are the two answers.
normal.cn: wh- 保留疑问，here 与 there 就是两种答案。

normal.en: Where is never were, though on paper the two are one letter apart in sound.
normal.cn: where 不是 were，尽管读音上两者只差一点。

normal.en: Somewhere, nowhere, anywhere: the same stem with a lid on top.
normal.cn: somewhere、nowhere、anywhere：同一个词干，上面加了不同的盖。

normal.en: In formal writing a where can mean a point in an argument, not only on a map.
normal.cn: 在正式文字中，where 可指论证中的一点，而不只地图上的位置。

abstract.en: Feel a fingertip on a folding map.
abstract.cn: 感觉指尖按在折叠地图上。

abstract.en: See a box put up high, out of reach.
abstract.cn: 看一只箱子被放到高处，够不到。

abstract.en: Hear your own village named out loud.
abstract.cn: 听别人念出你长大的村子。

examples.en: Where did you put the tickets?
examples.cn: 你把票放哪儿了？

examples.en: This is the street where my grandmother lived.
examples.cn: 这就是我祖母住过的那条街。

examples.en: Where possible, the report avoids technical words.
examples.cn: 在可能的地方，这份报告避免使用术语。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威尔」——威尔按着地图问：我到哪儿了？

root: 古英语 hwær（何处，hwa- 词干）→ 中古英语 where；同族有 whence、wherever、whereabouts。

sensesIntro.en: The word asks for a place, then links clauses to a place, then describes a named place, and finally points at an aspect of an argument.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先询问地点，再把从句系到地点上，随后描述已点明的地点，最后指向论证中的某个方面。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a fingertip pressed on one spot of a map.
core.cn: 核心意象：指尖压在地图的某一点上。

branches.en: The question branch: where is the key.
branches.cn: 提问分支：钥匙在哪儿。

branches.en: The clause branch: where the children cannot reach.
branches.cn: 从句分支：孩子够不到的地方。

branches.en: The relative branch: the village where she grew up.
branches.cn: 关系分支：她长大的村子。

branches.en: The abstract branch: where the cost is concerned.
branches.cn: 抽象分支：在花费方面。

branches.en: The family branch: somewhere, nowhere and anywhere reuse the stem.
branches.cn: 词族分支：somewhere、nowhere、anywhere 复用同一词干。

intro.en: Where is a free Germanic stem, and its family is built with ever, about and with the combining words some, any and no.
intro.cn: where 是自由的日耳曼语词干，其词族用 ever、about 以及 some、any、no 等构词成分扩展。

latinIntro.en: Latin asked the place with ubi and quo, short particles rather than compounds; the entries below are the borrowed parallels.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 ubi 与 quo 这类短小虚词询问地点，而非复合词；下面条目是并行说法。

items.example: It works as adverb, conjunction and relative word.
items.exampleCN: 它可作副词、连词和关系词。

items.example: It began as where plus so.
items.exampleCN: 它本是 where 加 so。

items.meaning: in the cases that allow it
items.example: It carries the word into abstract ground.
items.exampleCN: 它把这个词带入抽象地带。

definition_zh: 是否；不管…（还是…）；会不会（两件事中的哪一件）
definition_en: used to introduce two or more possibilities, especially a yes or a no, when the answer is not known
core_image: 岔路口立着一块牌子，一边写「是」一边写「否」
scene: 车停在岔路口，司机摇下车窗问路，路边只有一块牌子：一边是「是」，一边是「否」。I do not know whether he will come tomorrow.
sceneCN: 这里 whether 是「是否」（第 1 个义项：引出知道与否尚未确定的一件事）；句意为我不知道他明天是否会来。岔路口一边「是」一边「否」的牌子就是这个词的印象。

collocations.zh: 不管是出于偶然还是有意

senses.title: Yes or no
senses.definition: used to name two choices, usually whether something is so and whether it is not
senses.definitionCN: 引出两个选择，通常指某事成立与不成立
senses.example: I do not know whether he will come tomorrow.
senses.exampleCN: 我不知道他明天是否会来。
senses.why: The word began as the Old English interrogative about two things, and the yes-or-no branch is the same fork seen without an answer.
senses.whyCN: 这个词源于古英语对两件事物的疑问，是与否两岔就是同一个岔口，只是没有答案。

senses.title: Either of two
senses.definition: used before two alternatives to say that neither one changes the result
senses.definitionCN: 用在两个并列选项前，表示两者都不改变结果
senses.example: Whether by accident or design, the paper arrived on the very last day.
senses.exampleCN: 不管是偶然还是有意，论文恰好在最后一天到了。
senses.why: When the two branches both lead to the same outcome, the fork stops being a question and becomes a condition.
senses.whyCN: 当两条岔路通向同一结果时，岔口不再问句，而成了一个条件。

senses.title: The question of if
senses.titleCN: 会不会；是否如此（作疑问的名词从句）
senses.definition: used after a verb of asking, knowing or doubting to introduce the matter in doubt
senses.definitionCN: 用在询问、知道、怀疑等动词之后，引出存疑的那件事
senses.example: They are still arguing about whether the plan is legal.
senses.exampleCN: 他们仍在争论这个计划是否合法。
senses.why: A reported question loses its question mark, and whether is the word left holding the doubt.
senses.whyCN: 转述的问句丢掉了问号，whether 就成了那个承载疑问的词。

intro.en: Whether is the Old English pair hwæther or hwæder, which of two, and it has kept that fork-shaped meaning for more than a thousand years.
intro.cn: whether 源自中古前的古英语 hwæther / hwæder（两者中的哪一个），一千多年里一直保留这种分岔的意义。

items.en: The stem hwa- asked about a pair, unlike the plain what that asked about any thing.
items.cn: 词干 hwa- 问的是一对中的哪一个，与询问任何事物的 what 不同。

items.en: Hwæther was the word for which of the two, and it could open a question or a clause.
items.cn: hwæther 是「两者中哪一个」的说法，既能开启问句，也能引出一个从句。

items.en: The final r weakened and was often dropped before a consonant, which gave the modern spelling and pronunciation.
items.cn: 词尾的 r 变弱，在辅音前常被吞掉，于是形成今天的拼写与读音。

items.en: The fixed pair whether or no (later whether or not) settled the alternative pattern in print.
items.cn: 固定的搭配 whether or no（后来作 whether or not）把这种两选句式固定在书面语里。

items.en: Grammar books sorted whether and if apart, keeping whether for careful writing and after prepositions.
items.cn: 语法书把 whether 与 if 分工，让 whether 留在严谨的文章和介词之后。

note.en: The first group collects the words that share the same wh shape, the second the words that also offer a choice or a condition.
note.cn: 第一组收与它字形相近的 wh 词，第二组收同样引出选择或条件的说法。

entries.definition: Not a question word at all, but the state of the sky.
entries.definitionCN: 天气（与 whether 读音几乎相同）

entries.definition: To dry up and shrink, one vowel apart.
The old word for to what place.
A different opening letter, meaning to a certain degree.
Can also mean whether, but never after a preposition.
One of the two, the older partner of whether.
Marks a doubt instead of naming the two branches.
Covers the either-or sense: it does not matter which.

normalIntro.en: Think of a road sign with two arrows, one saying yes and one saying no, and the word is the sign itself.
normalIntro.cn: 想一块画着两支箭头、一支写「是」一支写「否」的路牌，这个词就是那块牌子。

normal.en: Whether and weather sound the same, but one asks about a choice and one about the sky.
normal.cn: whether 与 weather 同音，但一个问选择，一个说天空。

normal.en: Whether or not: the or not is the second branch, made explicit.
normal.cn: whether or not：那个 or not 就是把第二条岔路说出来。

normal.en: After a preposition only whether works, as the decision was about whether to go.
normal.cn: 介词之后只能用 whether，例如决定是关于要不要去。

normal.en: The th in the middle links it to other and either, its old partner.
normal.cn: 中间那个 th 把它与 other、either 这些老伙伴连在一起。

normal.en: If two branches end in the same place, the question becomes a concession.
normal.cn: 若两条岔路通向同一处，疑问就变成让步。

abstract.en: See a fork in a road with no map.
abstract.cn: 想一个没有地图的岔路口。

abstract.en: Hear two arrows pointing opposite ways.
abstract.cn: 听两支箭头指向相反方向。

abstract.en: Feel the doubt of a question that expects no answer.
abstract.cn: 感受一个并不期待回答的疑问。

examples.en: Please tell me whether the shop is still open.
examples.cn: 请告诉我那家店是否还开着。

examples.en: Whether she likes it or not, the rules must be followed.
examples.cn: 不管她喜不喜欢，规则都必须遵守。

examples.en: The only question is whether we have enough time.
examples.cn: 唯一的问题是时间够不够。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「喂泽」——站在岔路口朝两边各喂一声：去还是不去？

root: 古英语 hwæther / hwæder（两者中的哪一个）→ 中古英语 whether；同族有 either、other、whither。

sensesIntro.en: The word is born as a question about two things, turns into a neither-one-matters concession, and finally becomes the standard carrier of doubt.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词生来就是对两个事物的疑问，转成「哪个都无所谓」的让步，最后成为承载疑问的标准说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a signpost with a yes arrow and a no arrow.
core.cn: 核心意象：一块写着「是」与「否」两支箭头的路牌。

branches.en: The fork branch: he will come or he will not.
branches.cn: 岔路分支：他会来，或者不会来。

branches.en: The concession branch: whether by accident or design.
branches.cn: 让步分支：不管是偶然还是有意。

branches.en: The doubt branch: arguing about whether the plan is legal.
branches.cn: 存疑分支：争论计划是否合法。

branches.en: The grammar branch: whether after a preposition, never if.
branches.cn: 语法分支：介词之后用 whether，不用 if。

branches.en: The writing branch: careful prose keeps the full word.
branches.cn: 书面分支：严谨文章保留完整的词形。

intro.en: Whether is an old whole word, but its endings and its partners are transparent enough to take apart.
intro.cn: whether 是一个古老的整体词，不过它的词尾与搭档足够透明，可以拆开来看。

latinIntro.en: Latin marked a fork with utrum for the question and sive for the alternatives; the entries below are the borrowed counterparts, not ancestors of whether.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 utrum 表示疑问的分岔，用 sive 表示并列的选项；下面的条目是借入的对应词，并非 whether 的祖先。

items.example: It carries a fork in one word.
items.exampleCN: 它把岔口装在一个词里。

items.example: The same ending shows in other and either.
items.exampleCN: 同样的词尾出现在 other 和 either 中。

items.example: It answers the fork of whether.
items.exampleCN: 它回答了 whether 那个岔口。

items.example: It shares the ancient th ending.
items.exampleCN: 它共用了古老的 th 词尾。

items.example: It keeps the old wh question.
items.exampleCN: 它保留了古老的 wh 疑问。

items.example: It spells out the second branch.
items.exampleCN: 它把第二条岔路说出来。

items.example: It is the older and shorter form.
items.exampleCN: 这是更早也更短的形式。

items.example: It follows verbs such as decide.
items.exampleCN: 它跟在 decide 这类动词之后。

definition_zh: 哪一个；（关系代词）…的那个；（用于指前面整件事）这一点
definition_en: used to ask about one member of a known set, or to add information about a thing just named
core_image: 一排编号的抽屉，手指停在其中一个上面
scene: 抽屉柜前站着一排人，教练伸手在编号的抽屉上逐个点过，最后停在第三个上。Which of these bags is yours?
sceneCN: 这里 which 是「哪一个」（第 1 个义项：在已知的一组事物里问是哪一件）；句意为这些包里哪个是你的。手指在一排编号抽屉上逐个点过的动作就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: One out of a known set
senses.definition: used in a question to ask which member of a group or list is meant
senses.definitionCN: 在问句中询问某组或某份清单中的哪一个成员
senses.example: Which of these bags is yours?
senses.exampleCN: 这些包里哪个是你的？
senses.why: The oldest job of the word is to narrow a set down to one member, and that is still the core of it.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的任务就是把一组缩小成某一个成员，这至今仍是它的核心。

senses.title: The thing that
senses.definition: used after a noun to introduce a clause that identifies or describes that noun
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词之后，引出对那个名词加以限定或描述的从句
senses.example: The book which she lent me is on the desk.
senses.exampleCN: 她借给我的那本书在桌上。
senses.why: A question about which member was reused as the link that points back to the member already chosen.
senses.whyCN: 询问哪一个成员的问句被借来作连接，指回已经被选定的那个成员。

senses.title: The whole fact
senses.definition: used with a comma to comment on the whole of what has just been said
senses.definitionCN: 与逗号连用，对刚说过的整件事发表评论
senses.example: He arrived two hours late, which annoyed everyone.
senses.exampleCN: 他迟到两小时，这让大家都恼火。
senses.why: Once the clause can point back to a thing, it easily points back to an entire statement.
senses.whyCN: 从句一旦能指回一个事物，就很容易再指回整段陈述。

intro.en: Which is the Old English interrogative hwylc, a compound of hwa (who, what) and a suffix meaning like, so it began as what sort of.
intro.cn: which 是古英语疑问词 hwylc，由 hwa（谁、什么）与表示「像…那样」的词尾复合而成，本义是「什么样的」。

items.en: The stem hwa- asked about persons and things, and the compound added the idea of a kind.
items.cn: 词干 hwa- 询问人与事物，复合之后又加上「种类」的意思。

items.en: Hwylc meant what kind of and was used to pick one thing out of a set.
items.cn: hwylc 意为「什么样的」，用来从一组中挑出一件。

items.en: The spelling settled as which, and the word took on the relative job alongside that.
items.cn: 拼写固定为 which，这个词除了 that 之外还承担了关系词的职能。

items.en: Writers began to split which for things and who for people, though the choice was still loose.
items.cn: 作者们开始让 which 指物、who 指人，尽管这种分工当时还不严格。

items.en: Modern usage lets which point back to a whole sentence, a use that who cannot take.
items.cn: 现代用法允许 which 指回整个句子，而 who 无法这样用。

note.en: The first group is the wh question family, the second the relatives that link a clause to a noun.
note.cn: 第一组是 wh 疑问词家族，第二组是连接从句与名词的关系词。

entries.definition: Asks with no list to choose from.
Same sound, no question at all.
The same family narrow to people.
Which, widened to any member.
The other common relative, more often for defining clauses.
The relative for people.
The object form, kept for formal prose.
Which plus a place, in the older grammar.

normalIntro.en: Which always works inside a set: point at the members first, then let the word choose one.
normalIntro.cn: which 总在一个集合里工作：先点出各个成员，再让这个词挑出一个。

normal.en: What opens the question; which opens the list.
normal.cn: what 打开问题，which 打开名单。

normal.en: The ch at the end is the same shape as a hand picking.
normal.cn: 词尾的 ch 像一只手在挑选。

normal.en: Add ever and no member can be left out: whichever.
normal.cn: 加上 ever，就没有成员能被排除：whichever。

normal.en: After a comma it can comment on the whole sentence.
normal.cn: 在逗号之后，它可以评论整个句子。

normal.en: The which of a choice and the which of a relative are the same pointing finger.
normal.cn: 选择里的 which 和关系词里的 which 是同一根手指在指。

abstract.en: See numbered drawers and one finger moving along them.
abstract.cn: 想一排编号的抽屉和一根移动的手指。

abstract.en: Hear the short stop of a choice being made.
abstract.cn: 听做出选择时那一下短促的停顿。

abstract.en: Feel the narrowed field of a list instead of an open space.
abstract.cn: 感受名单收窄的场域，而不是一片空地。

examples.en: Which train goes to the airport?
examples.cn: 哪趟车去机场？

examples.en: This is the house which my grandfather built.
examples.cn: 这是我祖父盖的那座房子。

examples.en: She missed the last bus, which made her late.
examples.cn: 她错过了末班车，这让她迟到了。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「威吃」——一堆包里只要吃的那一包，得先问：哪一个？

root: 古英语 hwylc（什么样的，由 hwa 与 -lic 复合）→ 中古英语 which；同族有 what、who、whichever。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts by narrowing a set to one member, turns that question into a relative link, and finally learns to point back at a whole statement.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词先把一组缩小到某一位成员，再把那个问句变成关系连接，最后学会指回整段陈述。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a finger moving along numbered drawers.
core.cn: 核心意象：一根手指沿着一排编号抽屉移动。

branches.en: The question branch: which of these bags is yours.
branches.cn: 问句分支：这些包里哪个是你的。

branches.en: The relative branch: the book which she lent me.
branches.cn: 关系分支：她借给我的那本书。

branches.en: The people branch: which for things, who for people.
branches.cn: 指人分支：which 指物，who 指人。

branches.en: The comment branch: which annoyed everyone.
branches.cn: 评论分支：这让大家都恼火。

branches.en: The derived branch: whichever covers every member.
branches.cn: 派生分支：whichever 覆盖每一个成员。

intro.en: Which is an old compound of the interrogative stem and a kind suffix, and it still takes ever and so as partners.
intro.cn: which 是疑问词干与「种类」词尾构成的古老复合词，今天仍以 ever、so 为搭档。

latinIntro.en: Latin used quis or qui for which, and the entries below are the borrowed roots rather than ancestors of which.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 quis、qui 表示「哪个」，下面的条目是借入的词根，而非 which 的祖先。

items.example: It opens the whole wh family.
items.exampleCN: 它开启了整个 wh 家族。

items.example: It widens the choice to all.

items.exampleCN: 它加强 whichever 的语气。

items.example: It uses which as a link.
items.exampleCN: 它把 which 用作连接。

items.example: It shows which after a preposition.
items.exampleCN: 它显示 which 出现在介词之后。

items.example: It keeps the old kind suffix.
items.exampleCN: 它保留了古老的种类词尾。

definition_zh: 当…的时候；虽然；然而；（一段时间）一会儿
definition_en: during the time that something happens, and also used to contrast two facts or to name a short period of time
core_image: 两条平行的钟表指针同时走着，一条走完另一条还在动
scene: 厨房里水在烧，她一边等一边切菜，两个动作同时进行。She read the paper while the water was boiling.
sceneCN: 这里 while 是「当…的时候」（第 1 个义项：在某事进行的那段时间里）；句意为水开的时候她在看报纸。两条平行走的指针同时指着的画面就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: During the time that
senses.definition: used to say that one thing happens during the same period as another
senses.definitionCN: 表示一件事与另一件事发生在同一段时间内
senses.example: She read the paper while the water was boiling.
senses.exampleCN: 水开的时候她在看报纸。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply a stretch of time, and a clause placed inside that stretch gives the during meaning.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的意思只是一段时间，把从句放进这段时间里就产生了「当…时」的意思。

senses.title: Although
senses.definition: used at the start of a clause to admit a fact that makes the main point surprising
senses.definitionCN: 用在从句开头，承认一个使主句令人意外的事实
senses.example: While the plan is cheap, it will take years to finish.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划虽然便宜，却要花好几年才能完成。
senses.why: Two things placed side by side invite comparison, and when the second weakens the first the word leans to although.
senses.whyCN: 两件事并排摆放就会引来比较，当第二件削弱第一件时，这个词便偏向 although。

senses.title: Whereas
senses.definition: used to compare two facts and show that they are different
senses.definitionCN: 比较两个事实，显示二者不同
senses.example: Some people talk a lot, while others say nothing.
senses.exampleCN: 有些人话很多，而另一些人什么都不说。
senses.why: The same side-by-side picture becomes a plain contrast when the two facts are simply weighed against each other.
senses.whyCN: 同样是并排的画面，当两个事实只是彼此对照时，就成了单纯的对比。

senses.title: A period of time
senses.definition: a short period of time, usually after the words a or for
senses.definitionCN: 一小段时间，通常跟在 a 或 for 之后
senses.example: Wait here for a while and I will be back.
senses.exampleCN: 在这里等一会儿，我就回来。
senses.why: This is the noun behind the conjunction: a while is the stretch of time that the clause later filled in.
senses.whyCN: 这是连词背后的名词：a while 就是后来被从句填进去的那段时间。

senses.title: To pass time pleasantly
senses.definition: in while away, to spend time in a relaxed way until it has passed
senses.definitionCN: 在 while away 中，指轻松地度过一段时间
senses.example: We whiled away the afternoon on the beach.
senses.exampleCN: 我们在海滩上打发了整个下午。
senses.why: If a while is a block of time, then while away is the act of letting that block be used up.
senses.whyCN: 如果 a while 是一块时间，那么 while away 就是让那块时间被用掉的动作。

intro.en: While began as the Old English noun hwīl, a period of time, and only later became the conjunction that fills such a period.
intro.cn: while 起初是古英语名词 hwīl（一段时间），后来才成为填充这段时间的连词。

items.en: The stem hwī- meant a rest or a span of time in the older Germanic languages.
items.cn: 在较早的日耳曼语中，词干 hwī- 指一段休息或一段时间。

items.en: Hwīl was a noun, and the phrase þā hwīle þe, the time that, was its full form.
items.cn: hwīl 是名词，完整形式是 þā hwīle þe，意思是「…的那段时间」。

items.en: The long phrase shrank to while that and then to plain while, which took over the conjunction job.
items.cn: 长短语缩短为 while that，再缩成 while，连词职能便由它承担。

items.en: While spread into contrast and concession, replacing older words in ordinary prose.
items.cn: while 扩展到对比与让步，在普通文章中取代了更早的说法。

items.en: The noun survives in a while, once in a while and while away, keeping the original time sense.
items.cn: 名词义保存在 a while、once in a while 与 while away 中，保留了最初的时间意味。

note.en: The first group is the words one letter away in shape, the second the time and contrast words that do the same work.
note.cn: 第一组是字形只差一点的词，第二组是承担同样职能的时间与转折词。

entries.definition: A very large sea animal, one letter longer.
The same word with a t, common in British prose.
A trick, and the same shape as the verb in while away.
A high complaining sound.
The preposition version of the same time relation.
Two things happening at the same moment.
The full concession word behind sense two.
The formal contrast partner of while.

normalIntro.en: Hold two films running side by side, and while is the word that ties their frames together.
normalIntro.cn: 想两部并排播放的影片，while 就是把两边的画面绑在一起的那个词。

normal.en: A while is a block of time, so the conjunction simply puts a clause inside the block.
normal.cn: a while 是一块时间，连词就是把从句放进这块时间里。

normal.en: Side by side can mean at the same time, in contrast, or in spite of.
normal.cn: 并排既可以是同时，也可以是对比，还可以是让步。

normal.en: While away means letting the block of time run out pleasantly.
normal.cn: while away 是让那块时间愉快地流走。

normal.en: British writing adds a t and says whilst; ordinary speech does not.
normal.cn: 英式书面语加个 t 说 whilst，日常口语则不这样用。

normal.en: After a comma, while begins the second of two weighed facts.
normal.cn: 在逗号之后，while 引出两个被比较事实中的第二个。

abstract.en: See two clock hands turning at the same pace.
abstract.cn: 想两根同时同速转动的钟表指针。

abstract.en: Hear water boiling under a quiet page turning.
abstract.cn: 听水开的声响下面是翻书声。

abstract.en: Feel a stretch of time with nothing urgent in it.
abstract.cn: 感受一段没有急事的时光。

examples.en: He called while I was cooking dinner.
examples.cn: 我做晚饭的时候他打来了电话。

examples.en: While I agree with you, I cannot support this plan.
examples.cn: 虽然我同意你的看法，却无法支持这个计划。

examples.en: Let us rest for a while before we continue.
examples.cn: 我们歇一会儿再继续吧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「外欧」——望外一瞧，时间悄悄流过去一会儿。

root: 古英语名词 hwīl（一段时间）→ 中古英语 while；同族有 whilst、meanwhile、worthwhile。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as a block of time, then fills that block with a clause, then weighs two clauses, and finally keeps the plain noun in a while and while away.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从一块时间开始，用从句把这块时间填满，再让两个从句相互权衡，最后把朴素的名词义留在 a while 与 while away 里。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two clock hands moving side by side.
core.cn: 核心意象：两根并排走动的钟表指针。

branches.en: The simultaneity branch: boiling water and a newspaper.
branches.cn: 同时分支：烧水与看报。

branches.en: The concession branch: while the plan is cheap, it is slow.
branches.cn: 让步分支：计划虽便宜，却很慢。

branches.en: The contrast branch: some talk, while others say nothing.
branches.cn: 对比分支：有人话多，有人沉默。

branches.en: The noun branch: wait for a while.
branches.cn: 名词分支：等一会儿。

branches.en: The phrasal branch: whiling away an afternoon.
branches.cn: 短语分支：打发一个下午。

intro.en: While is a free Old English word; its family is made by compounds such as meanwhile and by the old -st form whilst.
intro.cn: while 是古英语的自由词；它的词族由 meanwhile 这类复合词和古老的 -st 形式 whilst 构成。

latinIntro.en: Latin covered the same ground with dum and interim; the entries below are parallel forms, not the source of while.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 dum 与 interim 表达同样的意思；下面的条目是平行形式，并非 while 的来源。

items.example: It works as noun and conjunction.
items.exampleCN: 它既可作名词也可作连词。

items.example: It keeps the old noun alive.
items.exampleCN: 它让古老的名词义活下来。

items.example: It repeats the noun in idiom.
items.exampleCN: 它在习语中重复这个名词。

items.example: It turns time into a verb.
It is the bridge to the conjunction.

definition_zh: 白色；白色的；白人的；苍白；空白
definition_en: the colour of fresh snow or of milk, and anything of that colour, pale, or left blank
core_image: 院子里刚落下的一层雪，白得反光，连屋顶的边都看不清
scene: 清晨推门，院子里的雪一夜未动，白得刺眼，脚印一踩就留下深灰的坑。After the storm the hills were white as far as the eye could see.
sceneCN: 这里 white 是「白色」（第 1 个义项：雪或牛奶那样的颜色）；句意为风暴过后，目力所及的山全是白色。那层反光的、连屋顶边缘都看不清的雪，就是这个词的印象。

senses.title: The colour of snow
senses.definition: the lightest colour, the one that reflects almost all the light reaching it, like fresh snow or milk
senses.definitionCN: 最浅的颜色，几乎反射所有照来的光，如新雪或牛奶
senses.example: After the storm the hills were white as far as the eye could see.
senses.exampleCN: 风暴过后，目力所及的山全是白色。
senses.why: It is the colour with nothing added, the visual point where every other colour is absent.
senses.whyCN: 这是什么也不加的颜色，是其他颜色都不在场时的那一点。

senses.title: Very pale in the face
senses.definition: used of a face that has lost its natural colour through fear, illness or cold
senses.definitionCN: 形容脸色因恐惧、疾病或寒冷而失去血色
senses.example: She went white when the doctor read the result.
senses.exampleCN: 医生念出结果时，她的脸刷地白了。
senses.why: Blood leaving the skin leaves the same colour as snow behind, so the word doubles as a sign of shock.
senses.whyCN: 血液离开皮肤时留下的正是雪那样的颜色，于是这个词也成了惊吓的记号。

senses.title: A blank part
senses.definition: a space left empty on a printed page or a form, waiting to be filled
senses.definitionCN: 印刷页或表格上留出、等待填写的一块空地
senses.example: Write your answers in the white space below each question.
senses.exampleCN: 把答案写在每道题下面的空白处。
senses.why: An unprinted sheet is simply paper showing through, and paper at that time was white.
senses.whyCN: 未印字的纸页就是纸本身的颜色透出来，而当时的纸正是白的。

senses.title: The transparent part of an egg
senses.definition: the clear liquid around the yolk of an egg, which turns white when cooked
senses.definitionCN: 蛋中央蛋黄周围的透明液体，煮熟后变成白色
senses.example: Beat the whites of three eggs until they stand in soft peaks.
senses.exampleCN: 把三个蛋的蛋白打到能立起柔软的尖角。
senses.why: Raw it looks clear, cooked it turns white, so English named it for the state you see on the plate.
senses.whyCN: 生时透明，熟后变白，于是英语按盘中看到的样子给它命名。

senses.title: A group of people and their history
senses.definition: used of people with light skin, or of the social category built around them
senses.definitionCN: 指肤色浅的人，或围绕他们形成的社会类别
senses.example: The law treated white and black families very differently then.
senses.exampleCN: 那时法律对白人家庭和黑人家庭的处理大不相同。
senses.why: A colour word was placed on skin, and the label hardened into a social fact that has to be read with care.
senses.whyCN: 一个颜色词被贴到皮肤上，这个标签又固化成社会事实，使用时须格外谨慎。

intro.en: White comes from Old English hwit, which goes back to a Germanic root meaning bright or shining, not primarily a colour.
intro.cn: white 源自古英语 hwit，可上溯到表示「明亮、发亮」的日耳曼语词根，最初并不主要是颜色。

items.en: The old root meant bright and shining, the way light looks when it hits a smooth surface.
items.cn: 古老的词根表示明亮、发亮，即光打在光滑表面上呈现的样子。

items.en: Hwit described snow, milk, silver and hair, and also carried the sense of being pure or fortunate.
items.cn: hwit 描述雪、牛奶、银和白发，同时带有纯洁或幸运之意。

items.en: The spelling shifted to whit, whyt and finally white, while the h stayed silent after w.
items.cn: 拼写先后变为 whit、whyt，最后成为 white，而 w 之后的 h 始终不发音。

items.en: The word spread to faces, to eggs, to empty page space and to the colour of coffee with milk.
items.cn: 这个词扩展到脸色、蛋、书页空白以及加奶咖啡的颜色。

items.en: From the nineteenth century it was applied to skin and to whole populations, a use that carries a heavy social history.
items.cn: 自十九世纪起，它被用于肤色与整个族群，这一用法背负沉重的社会历史。

note.en: The first group gathers other colours that sit beside white, the second the words for paleness and for plainness.
note.cn: 第一组收与白色相邻的其他颜色，第二组收表示苍白与素净的说法。

entries.definition: The colour of coal, the darkest end of the scale.
The colour between black and white, like stone or cloud.
Light in colour, close to white but weaker.
The white stuff itself, a common way to picture white.
Left empty, with nothing written on it.
The quality of being clean and unmixed.
A soft white stone used for writing.

normalIntro.en: White is a colour word with a shining origin, so it should be remembered with light rather than with paint.
